limitations: resources/, scratch/, public/ were not cited as evidence by any of the 7 domain auditors: resources/ and public/ hold static build assets (icons, PWA manifest), scratch/ holds a dev scratch file (test-headers.js) — none flagged as risk, but none were positively inspected either, so outcome is honestly coverage-incomplete rather than rounded up.
No network access was available for this run (offline jCodeMunch profile, no package-manager execution): dependency versions were not checked against a live CVE/advisory database.
No test runner exists in the repository, so testing-domain findings rely entirely on static inspection; there is no execution-based coverage data to cross-check against.

jCodeMunch v1.108.291: repository-scoped exclude_skip_directories is ignored during traversal (known upstream limitation) — build/dependency directories were excluded via explicit extra_ignore_patterns at index time instead, and get_dead_code_v2 signal_warning (2 of 3 signals non-discriminating) meant that sweep was corroborated manually rather than trusted directly.

Individual auditors additionally scoped themselves narrower than the full repository for their own domain; those narrower self-reported scopes are recorded in each auditor own repodocs/audit/findings/<name>.json.
